appRouting.title: APP Rules
appRouting.appsHelp: One process name or full executable path per line. Add helper processes separately; a parent application does not automatically include its children.
appRouting.patternsHelp: Leave blank for all nodes, or enter one fancy-regex per line. Lookaround and backreferences are supported. Filters only list candidates; select a node manually. Excessive backtracking returns an error; nodes never switch automatically.
appRouting.unavailable: Not in the current candidate list
appRouting.ruleHelp: APP Rule mode copies the active profile's domain rules and proxy groups with independent node selections. Choose its nodes in Proxies → APP groups, separately from TUN Rule mode.
appRouting.manualOnly: Only the manually selected node is used. A failed, removed, or renamed node never causes an automatic switch to another node or Direct.
appRouting.missingNode: The selected node is missing from its original source. Its selection is retained and traffic is blocked until it returns or you manually select another node.
appRouting.outsideFilter: The selected node no longer matches these filters. Restore the filter or manually choose a different route.
appRouting.intro: APP routing is an independent TUN-only switch. Match an APP group first; otherwise use the normal Rule or Global exit. A pinned group never falls through to the default exit.
appRouting.inactive: APP routing is off. Saved groups are not applied; turn on APP to apply them without changing the default mode.
appRouting.nodesUnavailable: The node list is unavailable. Saved selections are retained; retry after the core is available.
appRouting.priority: Groups match from top to bottom; the first enabled group wins. Unmatched applications follow the mode selected on the Proxies page.
appRouting.empty: No APP groups yet. Start with a Browser group using Rule mode, or an AI group with a fixed residential node.
appRouting.failedNode: The latest node check timed out. This group will not switch automatically; select another node manually.
appRouting.connectionHelp: Changes apply to new connections. When “Close connections on mode change” is enabled, editing APP rules also reconnects existing traffic. Otherwise close old connections on the Connections page.
appRouting.deleteConfirm: Delete “{{name}}”? Its applications will use the next matching group or the normal default exit.
appRouting.directHelp: This group connects directly, without using proxy nodes or continuing through the original rules.
appRouting.runningAppsHelp: Select one or more programs. Processes using the same executable are combined; complete paths are saved when available. Open the program first if it is not listed.
appRouting.processListError: Could not read the program list. Refresh to retry.
appRouting.processNameFallback: Path unavailable; this entry will match the process name.
appRouting.noRunningApps: No matching programs. Start the program, then refresh.
appRouting.legacyDirect: This group uses the legacy Direct option. Choose Rule mode or Specific node before saving; the existing policy stays unchanged until then.
appRouting.tunDisabled: APP routing requires TUN enabled and system proxy disabled. Disabling TUN or enabling system proxy turns APP off without deleting groups.
appRouting.trafficHelp: Only TUN connections receive APP overrides; explicit HTTP/SOCKS proxy connections use the normal default mode. Loopback, known local domains and private/link-local destination addresses bypass proxy exits.
appRouting.groupsPageHelp: APP fixed nodes and independent Rule-mode proxy groups are managed here, separate from the TUN default.
appRouting.emptyGroupsPage: No APP groups yet. Create groups in APP Rules; subscription proxy groups are not displayed here.
appRouting.ruleGroupSummary: This group uses an independent copy of the domain rule chain. Select proxy nodes in the APP-only groups below; TUN selections remain unchanged.
appRouting.independentRuleHelp: These selectors have the same domain rules and group structure as the active profile, but independent node choices. Domain DIRECT rules still bypass the proxy; TUN nodes are unaffected.
appRouting.ruleGroupsUnavailable: No independent Rule-mode selectors are available. Enable TUN and APP routing, then refresh.
appRouting.groupClickHelp: One manually selected node is used for all applications in this group. An unavailable node never triggers automatic failover.
appRouting.noGroupNodes: No nodes match this group’s filters. Edit its filters in APP Rules or refresh the subscription.
appRouting.overlayHelp: APP overrides take priority for TUN traffic. Unmatched applications use the selected Rule, Global or Direct default exit.
appRouting.homeOverlayBrief: APP groups take priority; other traffic follows this mode.
appRouting.defaultModeHelp: Unmatched applications use {{mode}}. Matched APP groups retain their own exits.
